narrative: OMX30 faces a mixed open despite positive European correlation signals (+0.530%). European bourses rallied overnight on broad sentiment, but the NASDAQ's -1.25% decline and falling US 10Y yields (-87bp to 5.231%) create conflicting cues. Technicals show OMX30 in bull regime (+4.1% vs 200-MA) but critically weakened by ADX of just 7.0 (bearish directional bias) and MACD below signal. Copper strength (+2.82%) and gold rally (+1.17%) support commodity-linked exporters, yet the -0.5% gap below the 50-MA (3,180 level) signals near-term consolidation risk. With VIX lower at 15.16 and EUR/SEK down -0.27%, Swedish exporters face modest FX headwinds despite the broad risk-on tone.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens in a tug-of-war: European momentum (DAX/CAC up ~1.1%) versus NASDAQ weakness and falling yields. The index remains +4.1% above the 200-day MA (bullish structure) but sits -0.5% below the 50-MA at ~3,180—a key resistance to watch. ADX at 7.0 is critically weak, reducing confidence in any directional move; treat any rallies with caution for mean reversion. Copper outperformance (+2.82%) is a bright spot for Boliden and mining stocks, while gold's +1.17% gains add to that thesis. Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) face mixed signals: yields down is a NIM headwind, but lower rate expectations may ease refinancing pressure longer-term. Watch US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET for fresh direction. On weakness, support lies at 3,085 (lower Bollinger band); on strength, resistance at 3,180 (50-MA). Risk/reward is unfavorable until ADX recovers or a clear directional break forms.
